name: Vaibhav Naik
headline: Industrial & Systems Engineering
summary: I use process analysis, statistics, and production data to build more reliable manufacturing and operations systems. My focus is process quality, continuous improvement, and semiconductor manufacturing.

projects.title: Semiconductor Defect Analysis
projects.imageAlt: Illustrative wafer map and process-analysis concepts
projects.caption: Illustrative process visualization; not a measured wafer map.
projects.summary: A machine learning workflow and interactive dashboard for classifying wafer defects from process and inspection data.
projects.evidence: Synthetic sample data; implemented training and evaluation pipeline.
projects.problem: Early defect detection can help engineers investigate process excursions and protect wafer yield. This project examines whether process and inspection measurements can distinguish normal wafers from scratches, particles, edge-ring issues, and contamination.

approach.title: Prepare wafer features
approach.body: Combine numeric process measurements and categorical wafer information in a reproducible preprocessing pipeline.

approach.title: Train a baseline classifier
approach.body: Use a Random Forest model to classify defect types from the included synthetic sample dataset.

approach.title: Evaluate beyond accuracy
approach.body: Review holdout precision, recall, macro F1, a confusion matrix, and stratified cross-validation to understand class-specific performance.

approach.title: Make the analysis accessible
approach.body: Use a Streamlit dashboard to inspect the data, train the model, review feature importance, and explore single-wafer predictions.

projects.outcome: The repository contains the preprocessing, training, evaluation, and prediction workflow, along with a deployed dashboard. Performance metrics are generated when the model is trained; no production yield improvement is claimed.
projects.limitations: The included wafer data is synthetic. Feature importance is a model diagnostic and does not establish process causation. Production use would require real inspection data, validation across lots, and drift monitoring.
projects.next: Validate on real process data, compare model tuning strategies, and connect defect predictions to a wafer-yield investigation.

projects.title: SPC & Process Capability Dashboard
projects.imageAlt: Actual project screenshot showing statistical process control charts
projects.caption: SPC dashboard screenshot from the project repository.
projects.summary: A manufacturing test-bench analysis that brings control charts, capability, Pareto analysis, and FMEA into one dashboard.
projects.evidence: Public automotive manufacturing data; Define, Measure, and Analyze phases.
projects.problem: Test-bench cycle time can become a production constraint and a quality signal. This portfolio study uses the public Mercedes-Benz Greener Manufacturing dataset to investigate stability, variation, and configuration-level differences.

approach.title: Define the quality characteristic
approach.body: Treat test-bench duration as a critical-to-quality variable and make the study's specification window and target explicit.

approach.title: Check stability
approach.body: Compare I-MR, subgroup, EWMA, and CUSUM views with Western Electric and Nelson run-rule detection.

approach.title: Study capability and distribution
approach.body: Review capability indicators alongside the measured distribution. The repository identifies non-normality, so normal-model capability estimates need careful interpretation.

approach.title: Prioritize investigation
approach.body: Use configuration-level Pareto analysis, a structured fishbone, and FMEA to focus follow-up engineering work.

projects.outcome: The dashboard makes process excursions and configuration differences visible and documents the Define, Measure, and Analyze phases of DMAIC. Improvement pilots and sustained control validation remain future work.
projects.limitations: This is an independent study of a public competition dataset, not work performed for Mercedes-Benz. The specification window is an analytical assumption. Proposed corrective actions have not been validated in a production pilot.
projects.next: Design a focused experiment, validate proposed countermeasures, and document an operational control plan.

projects.title: Inventory Policy & Cost Optimization
projects.imageAlt: Actual inventory optimization dashboard with SKU analysis
projects.caption: Inventory dashboard screenshot from the project repository.
projects.summary: An EOQ and safety-stock model that translates retail transactions into SKU-level ordering policies and service-level tradeoffs.
projects.evidence: Public transactions; modeled policies and projected cost comparisons.
projects.problem: Inventory decisions must balance availability, ordering cost, and capital tied up in stock. This project uses public Online Retail transactions to develop reorder policies and identify high-value SKUs.

approach.title: Clean transaction history
approach.body: Remove cancellations, duplicates, non-positive quantities and prices, and non-product codes before modeling demand.

approach.title: Calculate ordering policies
approach.body: Estimate SKU-level demand, economic order quantity, safety stock, and reorder points under explicit cost and lead-time assumptions.

approach.title: Segment the portfolio
approach.body: Apply ABC classification to prioritize inventory attention using annual revenue contribution.

approach.title: Compare cost and service
approach.body: Compare the policy with a monthly-ordering baseline and examine how service level and lead time change inventory requirements.

projects.outcome: The repository documents policies for 3,659 SKUs from 391,150 modeled transactions, with an interactive dashboard and cost-sensitivity views. Savings are model projections against a defined baseline, not realized business savings.
projects.limitations: Ordering cost, holding cost, lead time, and service targets are assumptions because the transaction dataset does not contain those fields. The proposed policy needs operational validation.
projects.next: Validate lead-time and demand assumptions, add supplier constraints, and backtest stockout performance.

projects.title: Semiconductor Wafer Yield & Process Optimization
projects.summary: Investigate yield loss by tool and chamber, assess stability, and evaluate a more reliable operating window.
projects.evidence: Project scope defined; no measured results published yet.
projects.problem: A proposed wafer-process study will examine whether tool, chamber, and recipe differences explain a decline in yield.

approach.title: Establish the baseline
approach.body: Define wafer-level yield and defect measures, capture lot and tool identifiers, and distinguish real data from synthetic examples.

approach.title: Investigate variation
approach.body: Review trends, defect Pareto, tool/chamber comparisons, control charts, and capability under appropriate distribution assumptions.

approach.title: Test the process window
approach.body: Use a designed experiment to evaluate parameter interactions and validate a proposed recipe against an independent baseline.

projects.outcome: This page defines a future case study. Analysis artifacts, measured results, and a repository will be linked when available.
projects.limitations: No yield gains, capability improvements, or completed DOE results are claimed.
projects.next: Create a reproducible wafer-level dataset and document the initial yield baseline.

projects.title: Fab Scheduling & WIP Optimization
projects.summary: Compare dispatching rules, queue behavior, and bottleneck utilization in a simulated wafer-fab flow.
projects.evidence: Scheduling concept repository; fab simulation not implemented yet.
projects.problem: Re-entrant routes, variable tool availability, and priority lots make fab scheduling a tradeoff between throughput, cycle time, and due-date performance.

approach.title: Define the system
approach.body: Describe routes, lot sizes, tool capacity, setups, and assumptions about downtime.

approach.title: Compare policies
approach.body: Evaluate FIFO, shortest processing time, earliest due date, and bottleneck-aware rules under equivalent simulation conditions.

approach.title: Measure the tradeoffs
approach.body: Compare WIP, queue time, cycle time, utilization, and on-time completion across repeated simulation runs.

projects.outcome: The related repository currently describes a production-scheduling concept. No implemented fab simulation or validated lead-time reduction is presented.
projects.limitations: Expected improvements in the outline are targets rather than measured outcomes.
projects.next: Build a reproducible baseline model and add a scheduling comparison.

projects.title: Manufacturing DMAIC Defect Reduction
projects.summary: Extend a quality investigation through a validated improvement pilot and sustained control plan.
projects.evidence: Proposed improvement study; pilot and control validation pending.
projects.problem: A repeat manufacturing defect requires a measurable quality characteristic, a reliable baseline, and evidence that a corrective action addresses its cause.

approach.title: Define and measure
approach.body: Set the CTQ, scope, sampling plan, measurement-system checks, and baseline defect rate.

approach.title: Analyze and improve
approach.body: Prioritize defect modes with Pareto analysis, investigate causes, and test a focused corrective action.

approach.title: Sustain control
approach.body: Document an owner, monitoring frequency, reaction plan, and independent validation period.

projects.outcome: This study is planned. A future report will distinguish baseline performance, pilot effects, and sustained results.
projects.limitations: The existing SPC project provides analytical groundwork but does not establish a completed defect-reduction pilot.
projects.next: Choose a specific defect and establish a measurement plan.

projects.title: Production Line Balancing & Capacity Optimization
projects.summary: Study station workloads, compare cycle time with takt, and evaluate work allocation and capacity.
projects.evidence: Project scope defined; station measurements pending.
projects.problem: Uneven workloads can constrain a line even when total labor capacity appears adequate. This study will identify the limiting station and assess alternative allocations.

approach.title: Measure the current state
approach.body: Collect station times, demand, available production time, task precedence, and staffing constraints.

approach.title: Identify the constraint
approach.body: Compare cycle times with takt and calculate baseline capacity and balance delay.

approach.title: Evaluate a future state
approach.body: Assess task reallocation and staffing alternatives while preserving task precedence and required quality checks.

projects.outcome: A future analysis will include a line-balance chart, proposed allocation, and validated capacity comparison.
projects.limitations: No throughput, labor savings, or return-on-investment improvement is claimed before measurement.
projects.next: Collect a representative station-level time study.

projects.title: Manufacturing KPI & Quality Intelligence Dashboard
projects.summary: Connect production, defect, and downtime data into a practical view of manufacturing performance.
projects.evidence: Dashboard scope defined; manufacturing data model pending.
projects.problem: Separate production and quality reports make it difficult to see whether a performance issue comes from availability, operating speed, or defects.

approach.title: Define the data model
approach.body: Connect production, quality, and equipment facts with consistent lot, machine, product, shift, and date keys.

approach.title: Make measures consistent
approach.body: Specify denominators and time windows for first-pass yield, scrap, throughput, downtime, and OEE.

approach.title: Support decisions
approach.body: Create production and quality drilldowns, trends, and a documented approach to investigating exceptions.

projects.outcome: This planned project will produce a manufacturing data model, documented KPI definitions, and interactive reporting views.
projects.limitations: The dashboard has not yet been implemented. Example KPI values will be labeled as sample data.
projects.next: Create production, quality, and equipment tables and validate the KPI definitions.
